title: What If a Trash Fire Burned for Over 60 Years? Centralia's Did

scenes.text: What if a trash fire never went out? One has been burning since 1962.
In May 1962, garbage was burned in an old mine pit in Centralia, Pennsylvania. The flames reached a coal vein.
The fire spread underground and has burned for more than sixty years.
In 1981, a twelve-year-old boy fell into a sinkhole about four feet wide and 150 feet deep. He was pulled out alive.
Pennsylvania spent 42 million dollars relocating residents. About 1,400 lived there in 1962. Five remained by 2023.
Experts say the coal could keep it burning for up to 250 years.

description:
What if a trash fire never went out?
A fire that began in a Pennsylvania landfill in 1962 is still burning through coal under Centralia.
